newsitem.title: UK: Sterling gets support from strong UK M4 data.
newsitem.headline: Sterling gets support from strong UK M4 data.

text.p: Sterling firmed slightly to above 2.84 marks in Europe after UK M4 figures for May overshot forecasts, stepping up pressure for a further rate rise, said analysts.
Lending by British banks to consumers also surged in May.
Analysts said the 11.1 percent year-on-year rise in M4 money supply, which exceeded the predicted 10 percent rise, underlined strong retail sales data released on Wednesday.
"With such strong lending on the back of strong retail numbers, it's certainly going to put upward pressure on inflation expectations," said Nikko economist Simon Briscoe.
However, analysts did not envisage sterling rallying a great deal.
At 1000 GMT, sterling stood at 2.8385/92 marks, just below highs of 2.8430 marks after the M4 data, and 2.8382/87 late on Wednesday. Cable stood at $1.6414/24 against 1.6400/10.
"Sterling is quite well supported, largely in response to the strong retail data followed up by the M4 numbers this morning," said Brian Martin, chief forex economist at BZW.
"But with dollar/mark fairly rangebound it is difficult to see sterling/mark racing away."

Dollar/mark was under pressure after Germany's stronger-than-expected IFO survey and concerns over the Japan/U.S. trade gap which may surface at bilateral talks on Thursday ahead of the G7 summit in Denver, Colorado on Friday.
However any impact of the report, compiled by an independent British watchdog, is unlikely to kick in until after the budget, economists said.

"The report will be interesting as we could get a downward revision to the 2.5 percent assumed growth rate and consequently wider PSBR numbers in the future," said BZW's Martin. "But it's unlikely to have an immediate effect on sterling."
Analysts have speculated that Brown may use the findings to justify raising taxes in his July budget.
"We'll have to see what fiscal tightening we get - if it's judged to be insufficient there may be a greater need for a tightening of monetary policy," said Metcalfe.
He said any signs of further rate hikes would give sterling a short-term boost.
The pound strengthened earlier this month after the Bank of England, exercising its newly awarded independence, upped base rates a quarter point to 6.50 percent on June 6th.
